vulnerabilities.plainEnglish: Flask is a web server gateway interface (WSGI) web application framework. In versions 3.1.2 and below, when the session object is accessed, Flask should set the Vary: Cookie header., resulting in a Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability. The logic instructs caches not to cache the response, as it may contain information specific to a logged in user. This is handled in most cases, but some forms of access such as the Python in operator were overlooked. The severity and risk depend on the application being hosted behind a caching proxy that doesn't ignore responses with cookies, not setting a Cache-Control header to mark pages as private or non-cacheable, and accessing the session in a way that only touches keys without reading values or mutating the session. The issue has been fixed in version 3.1.3. This affects Flask 3.0.0. Upgrade to 3.1.3 or later to fix it.

posture.title: No SECURITY.md
posture.detail: There is no SECURITY.md telling people how to report a vulnerability.
posture.fix: Add a SECURITY.md with a contact address and a response timeframe.

posture.title: No Dependabot config
posture.detail: No .github/dependabot.yml was found, so dependency updates are not automated.
posture.fix: Add .github/dependabot.yml to get automated security update pull requests.

posture.title: .env file committed
posture.detail: An environment file is committed to the repo.
posture.fix: Remove it from the repo and git history, add .env to .gitignore, and rotate every credential in it.

posture.title: Vite dev server bound to 0.0.0.0
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo/vite.config.ts sets server.host to 0.0.0.0, exposing the dev server on the local network.
posture.fix: Restrict the dev server to localhost and review the plugins you install.

posture.title: Vite plugins in use
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo/vite.config.ts imports: vite, @vitejs/plugin-react. Review each plugin — a compromised or unmaintained plugin runs in your build.
posture.fix: Restrict the dev server to localhost and review the plugins you install.

posture.title: VITE_ variables are public by design
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo/vite.config.ts references VITE_API_URL. Anything prefixed VITE_ is baked into the client bundle — never put a secret behind that prefix.
posture.fix: Move real secrets out of VITE_ variables — use server-side secrets instead.

posture.title: Docker base image is not pinned to a version
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/Dockerfile uses node:latest as a base image with no pinned version (tag "latest" or no tag), so a rebuild can silently pull a different image.
posture.fix: pin the base image to a specific versioned tag, e.g. FROM node:20-alpine, and bump it deliberately.

posture.title: Possible secret passed as a Docker build argument
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/Dockerfile declares ARG API_TOKEN, a name that looks like a secret. Build arguments are stored in the image history and can be read back with docker history, so the value can leak to anyone who has the image.
posture.fix: pass the value with a BuildKit secret mount (RUN --mount=type=secret ...) instead, and never put it in an ARG or ENV.

posture.title: Dockerfile runs as root
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/Dockerfile sets USER root, so the container runs as root. If the application is compromised, the attacker has root inside the container.
posture.fix: create a dedicated non-root user in the Dockerfile (for example with a RUN step that adds the user) and switch to it with USER <username> before the final CMD.

posture.title: Dockerfile downloads a file with ADD
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/Dockerfile uses ADD to fetch https://example.com/releases/fake-app.tar.gz. ADD downloads the file without verifying a checksum, and its caching can silently reuse a stale copy.
posture.fix: use COPY for files from the build context, or download the file in a RUN step with curl and verify its checksum before using it.

posture.title: Kubernetes pod uses the host network
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/k8s/deployment.yaml sets hostNetwork: true, so the pod shares the host's network namespace and can see host network traffic and ports.
posture.fix: remove hostNetwork: true and expose the pod through a Service instead.

posture.title: Kubernetes container runs privileged
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/k8s/deployment.yaml sets privileged: true, giving the container full access to the host — effectively root on the node.
posture.fix: remove privileged: true and grant only the specific Linux capabilities the container needs.

posture.title: Kubernetes container runs as root (UID 0)
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/k8s/deployment.yaml sets runAsUser: 0, so the container runs as root.
posture.fix: set runAsUser to a non-zero UID, e.g. runAsUser: 1000, and make sure the image supports running as that user.

posture.title: Kubernetes container image is not pinned to a version
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/k8s/deployment.yaml runs container image myapp:latest with no pinned version (tag "latest" or no tag), so a redeploy can silently pull a different image.
posture.fix: pin the image to a specific versioned tag or a digest, e.g. image: myapp:1.2.3.

posture.title: Terraform provider random has no version constraint
posture.detail: tests/fixtures/fake-repo-tier3/main.tf uses provider random with no version constraint, so a future release of the provider can change your infrastructure on the next apply.
posture.fix: add a version constraint in the required_providers block, e.g. random = { source = "hashicorp/random", version = "5.0.0" }.
